newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria government preparing to buy cotton glut.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria government preparing to buy cotton glut.

text.p: Nigeria's military government is making preparations to buy a surplus of cotton on the market this year, the national news agency said on Tuesday.

The News Agency of Nigeria quoted agriculture minister Mohammed Gambo as saying discussions were under way with the finance ministry to make funds available to agricultural banks to pay for the excess cotton.
Gambo urged farmers not to panic as the government was making efforts to ensure they did not lose money.
Industry estimates put last year's Nigerian harvest at a little over 250,000 tonnes of seed cotton, which translates into about 90,000 tonnes of cotton lint after ginning.

But reports from the cotton region of northern Nigeria say a more farmers grew cotton in 1996. This was because a government subsidy on fertiliser had the effect of making it virtually unavailable, and cotton needs lower inputs than alternative crops.
Nigeria's cotton, which has a reputation for contamination with synthetic fibres from the sacks used to transport it, is largely used by local textile mills.
Due to economic recession, demand has slumped and left many mills running at as low as 20 percent capacity utilisation.
